thread:
sam: FYI seeing a ~25% throughput drop on the nf4 canary pool after the kernel-selector change. KV cache evictions spiked, memory +2GB on a few hosts.

jess: same here in us-west-2. tail latency up ~50-80ms. host churn +1.5x. :eyes:

rafael: I pulled a flamegraph — looks like prefetch worker threads are contending with the new kernel scheduler. lots of small batches getting scheduled, then falling back to slow path.

sam: interesting — did we change batching heuristics in the rollout? I thought that PR only touched kernel priority.

jess: PR 5893 changed min_batch_size from 1 -> 2 for nf4 when sequence_length > 512 (intended to reduce kernel swap freq). perhaps that interacts badly with prefetch.

rafael: exact symptom: kernel-selector prefers low-mem nf4-kernel-A for short context, but for mixed batches it flips to nf4-kernel-B which uses a fallback path. flip rate went from 3% -> 22% in perf trace.

profiler-bot: perf snapshot: https://perf.internal/reports/2143658700 (contains traces, kv-evict timeline)

sam: logs from one host: ```[2026-03-18T14:12:03Z] kv_cache: eviction spike: 146MB/s for 7s
[2026-03-18T14:12:03Z] kernel_selector: swapped kernel B <- A for batch 0x7f8
[2026-03-18T14:12:04Z] prefetch: queued 12 requests, worker 3 busy
```

mei: quick thought — the kernel-selection hotcache uses a TTL + LRU of 10s. If selection flips often, we thrash the KV cache because kernels have different KV layouts. Could be the root.

rafael: agree. hypothesis: the selector change introduced a quantile-based heuristic that biases towards NF4-B on 95th-percentile seqs; mixing short + long in same micro-batch causes oscillation.

sam: actionable? revert selector or force kernel pin for nf4 canary?

mei: I'd prefer a minimal mitigation: 1) pin kernel by workload for 30m on canary, 2) revert min_batch_size bump, 3) run a calibration sweep that measures kernel mismatch penalty for mixed batches.

jess: pinning command: `redwoodctl set-annotation pool/usw2 kernel-pin=nf4-A --duration=30m` — I can run that now if we agree.

rafael: also add a quick telemetry delta to capture per-batch kernel flip count. current metrics only track host-level flips. need per-batch to confirm. small patch ready.

sam: go ahead jess on pin. rafael, open the telemetry PR and tag me. I'll prepare a short rollback patch for the batching heuristic.

deploy-bot: canary pin applied to pool/usw2 by jess at 2026-03-18T14:18:20Z.

profiler-bot: started continuous sampling (30s window) for pools: usw2, use-east. report updating in perf dashboard.

jess: after pin: initial numbers look better. throughput +18% on pinned hosts, KV evict back down. still collecting 10m window.

sam: great. once telemetry confirms we'll roll the rollback for the batch-size change. also add a test in the integration harness to mix short+long seqs and assert no kernel flips in >95% of batches.

mei: noted for test. I'll draft the calibration sweep params: vary min_batch_size in [1,2,4], force kernel pin/no-pin, and measure per-token latency + kv-evict.

rafael: timeline: telemetry PR -> 1h, rollback patch -> 30m review, calibration sweep -> 3h run. aiming to be fully rolled back or mitigated within 6 hours.

sam: thanks team. low-chatter channel update in 30m with the numbers. :thumbsup:
